comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–2027 curriculum; Dutch part-time target, six-year recommended pacing
comparator.sourceNotes: The permanent target remains the Dutch part-time offering, not a separate English or full-time degree. Annex 1 supplies the selected comparative Religie en Levensbeschouwing route: ten 6-EC units in academic stage 1, ten 6-EC positions in stage 2, and 30-EC minor/profiling plus five 6-EC units in stage 3. Academic-stage totals are 60+60+60=180; the part-time table distributes these over six calendar years at 36,24,36,24,36,24 EC. The current route name is not conflated with the differently described Zingeving, geestelijke verzorging en samenleving programme starting in 2027. Article 10.4 specifies Dutch instruction in the first two academic stages, some English courses, and English instruction in the selected third stage; normalized instruction metadata includes NLD and ENG while raw Dutch provenance is retained. Four restricted positions are instantiated using the first-listed eligible alternative in each period, independently of UCR fit. Alternatives are not stacked. The 30-EC minor remains generic: Article 12.1 allows a qualifying minor or approved academic courses (at least 12 EC level 300), or placement up to 12 EC plus 18 EC courses; applicable approval, entry and non-overlap rules remain. The 0-EC Dutch test is embedded in Geschiedenis van de Wereldfilosofie, not added as credit. Research Lab: Preparation Thesis requires 120 EC, the analytic-methodologies lab follows participation in preparation, and the thesis follows completed preparation. Adopted current rules establish a pathway, not guaranteed future timetable availability. Re-audit 17 October 2026 reopens and confirms the adopted route/credits and part-time table directly. Current marketing redirects to a programme explicitly starting in 2027; it is not substituted for the 2026–2027 route. Article 9.1 additionally requires completion of all first-stage and first-semester second-stage units before preparation; its 120-EC threshold is not the sole condition. Current course-level pages independently checked for world philosophy, myth/ritual and Social Sciences. Social Sciences is substantive religion-focused theory, not a generic methods module; it remains unmatched.

core: Philosophical questions of meaning, belief, ethics and worldviews
Religious myths, texts, images and cultural identities
Religion, communities, institutions and public life
questions: How do people construct, interpret and contest meaning in cultural and public life?

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
trace: Mandatory first-year academic and personal formation.
Teaches legal systems, justice and law/society relations; provides the formal foundation for comparative constitutional study.
Studies Aquinas, natural law, rights and historical/philosophical justifications, contributing concrete value-and-authority inquiry.
Examines constitutional values, state institutions and religious constitutions through a comparative legal approach; no theology curriculum is inferred.
Examines knowledge, the existence of god, meaning, responsibility and philosophical argument.
Supplies explicit moral theories and applied ethical reasoning; not comparative religious ethics.
Examines self and personal identity, including Buddhist thought, alongside mind and consciousness.
Examines the nature and rationality of emotion and its relation to ethics and art; contributes philosophical inquiry into affect and value, not psychology of religion.
Studies freedom, luck, time and the self as substantive philosophical questions of agency and responsibility.
Examines authority, freedom, equality, pluralism and multiculturalism as frameworks for shared public life.
Studies ideological conflict, grievances, reconciliation and conflict transformation as a defined public-life context, without relabelling it religious conflict.
Supplies sociological theories of institutions, social relations, race, class and gender for the belief-and-public-life strand.
Teaches qualitative design, collection and interpretation of empirical social data; supplies an actual research method.
Studies modernity, imperialism and colonial responses as substantive contexts of social and cultural meaning.
Studies civil society, solidarity, the public sphere and empirical inquiry with civic organisations; not sociology of religion as a specialist course.
Studies social influences on thoughts, beliefs and behaviour; supports a specific social account of belief without claiming psychology of religion.
Examines material production in relation to religious, social and gendered identities across ancient societies.
Studies religious, cultural and social meaning in western-African visual traditions and the ethics of collection and repatriation.
Studies Renaissance art through cross-cultural exchange, including Islamic courts; contributes a defined artistic context rather than Islamic theology.
Examines Athenian democracy intertwined with myth and religion, its material expression and political participation.
Teaches interpretation of literary forms and narratives, providing tools for the text-and-meaning strand.
Studies literary representations of organised religion, duty, freedom and community within a wider literary history.
Directly compares mythic narratives across ancient, Indian, Byzantine and Arabic traditions, text and image.
Teaches humanist, feminist, Marxist, cultural-minority and psychoanalytic interpretations and a text-based research project.

selection.assessment: One complete broader response is justified by philosophical meaning, myth/text/image interpretation and belief in public life, with concrete complementary social, legal and qualitative methods study. The former no-match imposed an overly narrow all-religion-content test: it correctly identified specialist gaps, but those gaps do not invalidate this differently organised related-fields programme. Religion/political conflict would mostly relabel the same social/public-life strand; sustainability courses do not establish the religious-environment interaction needed for a separate religion-centred direction. Biblical/confessional and Islamic candidates require sustained source interpretation, theology and related languages that the documented UCR offerings cannot implement; generic humanities are not relabelled to fill them. These directions are independently considered, not excluded by the absence of a degree title or professional licence. One programme is retained; no second is manufactured.

alternatives.label: Philosophy, myth & cultural meaning
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has substantial philosophy, literary interpretation and material/religious-cultural study, complemented by social belief, law and public life. It is a broader related response, not a UCR theology or comparative-religion major.
alternatives.concept: Philosophy explores meaning, ethics and the self, while literature, myth and heritage examine how cultures express and interpret those questions. Social psychology, sociology, law and political thought connect belief and values to shared public life. This is a broader response rather than a specialist theology or comparative-religion curriculum.
progression: Western philosophy, sociology and literary study precede advanced self/emotion, social theory and interpretation. Archaeology and African heritage precede ancient-democracy study. Law, Society & Justice precedes constitutional law. All courses meet formal prerequisite and term availability constraints; advanced courses are supported by relevant earlier foundations where available.

blocks: Important partial overlap in the history and methods of philosophical argument; UCR is Western-focused, not the full world-philosophy scope.
Important direct overlap in comparative myth and its transmission through narratives and images. UCR is literary rather than a full religious-ritual course.

notes.text: VU offers sustained study of religious traditions, religious experience, sacred-text interpretation and religion-specific research. The UCR programme connects philosophy, myth, heritage and social life; it does not reproduce that specialist sequence or confer theological, ministry or spiritual-care qualifications. VU’s required thesis differs from the separately displayed optional UCR research opportunity.

audience.programmeDescription: Theology and Religious Studies at VU Amsterdam examines religious traditions, beliefs, texts and practices, and their place in society. This comparison uses the 2026–2027 Religion and Worldviews route, which combines study of several traditions with philosophy, social perspectives and research. The selected offering is part-time.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers a broader combination of philosophy, myth, cultural interpretation and belief in public life. It does not reproduce VU’s sustained study of religious traditions, sacred texts and religion-specific research. Shared rows indicate limited content relationships; blank cells preserve important differences. The UCR programme is not professional training for ministry or spiritual care.
